name: KCC-20 reference actor (argent-lang/kcc20-reference c8a0871, KCC20PublicMint app)

review.note: The official KCC-20 reference app linked from kcc-0020.md (argent-lang/kcc20-reference c8a0871, fixtures/public-mint/artifact.json, generator argentc 0.1.0): the KCC20 actor and the two issuers that share its covenant family, reviewed 2026-10-21 from chain bytes, an instruction-by-instruction reading and the real engine. Commits: this pin covers c8a0871. The KCC20 actor is byte-identical at b782466 and 27f8403 (the repository head on 2026-10-21), so every KCC20 fact here holds for a build of the current head. b782466 rebuilt both issuers with one added owner-signed entry, rebalance_value(sig) on tag 498fa185, which keeps the issuer's state field for field and changes only its KAS value: PublicMint 8c87ce6e88755277... (2,074 B, window 1+150) and TokenSeed 6ea2c53a45cc4dcd... (1,408 B, window 1+132). This pin does not cover those two rebuilt issuers: no reveal of either was on chain at review time (a full sweep of the 2026-10-18 mainnet and 2026-10-19 testnet-10 copies, an indexed live lookup on 2026-10-21), so they have no bytes-to-chain leg yet. Their artifact bytes were exercised on the engine all the same, every issuer rule below and rebalance_value check by check. Bytes to chain: the KCC20 fixtures are leader reveals (tag 79c71c23) fetched from chain. A is mainnet 7d424a92d5157e2bd96986ce36cf9df43ddb499c16226ceb3cc574265e434f43:0, the genesis cell of the first mainnet reference token (covenant e9baad99...), revealed by 2a1ce33551b7e416c3407f894d0c93c5516e7e35a677f174f397fd260519b3dd input 0; B is testnet-10 05060a38b57f94c2c6f75535b99cef92539a82731e5e1e08845801038d81bdd8:1 (covenant df170857...), seeded by TokenSeed.create and revealed by f13f6ce015526d006742f3cdedba4608ecf33381196d2eeac30f5de8d976f71c input 0. They differ in all six record fields, the class included (all-zero against 77545d3d...), so the pin does not need fixtures_share_class. The issuer fixtures are testnet-10 reveals: PublicMint ec214f90d2b454cdc0f99cf87de75af61b9dd5882401c2f938f5aaf7ba2bf19d:0 (mint, tag 0fe04b09, by 7fa12aa5536a6a05ac9171d03c493d912a40a785fe2c953e231fbb7f7fd5bf59 input 0) and 0f6a30b3b5a6b3b086b759a26db094513aeb3b6bc1239860963994f58c0466de:0 (mint by d810a15d1c470f700f66fc86c7be84f33f21f2f59d3217fe4313bc6f366c9722 input 0); TokenSeed ec214f90...:1 (create, tag d1f8dfa0, by 05060a38... input 0) and 0f6a30b3...:1 (create by e2396f7b70f0d571405bdfc67000b1b76d93ea259f737a62e2aed03dfef1eba7 input 0). Each fixture is the last push of its spending signature script and its blake2b is the P2SH commitment it spent. A sweep of every spent covenant output on both copies found 144 KCC20 reveals on mainnet and 23,991 KCC20, 12,532 PublicMint and 10 TokenSeed reveals on testnet-10, each the artifact's bytecode byte for byte outside its window and each recomputing 9703112e, 14b0f06b or f79a3fcc; every successor a leader or an issue declared (197 on mainnet, 31,388 on testnet-10) rebuilds from the artifact to its output's commitment. The KCC20 window is the actor's own template hash (gen__kcc20_template, one 32-byte push at R[1..34]) followed by the 112-byte KCC20State (R[34..146]), so the record sits at offset 33; the canonical hash is taken around the whole window and the record view around the record alone (734850b0..., the artifact's actor_type_handle), both required. The window's end is also proven from the program's own bytes: 4031 is pushed three times and -3885 three times (one pair per output slot) and 3885 twice, and every continuation is rebuilt from the active input's own signature script as R[0..1] and the 3,885-byte suffix around a state the program encodes itself. Bytes: every arm of the three actors was read instruction by instruction against contracts/kcc20.ag and the generated sil/KCC20.sil, and every field of this pin matches the bytecode. KCC20.transfer (79c71c23): the leader is the family's first input; one or two delegates, each authenticated as this template by its P2SH and its template hash and required to carry the leader's extension commitment; one to three family outputs, all authorised by the leader and equal in number to next_states; every successor amount non-negative, owner scheme 0x00-0x04, borrow scheme 0x00-0x03 and the leader's extension commitment; the input total equal to the output total in checked i64; a first witness byte 0x00 for owner authorization or 0x01 for a borrowed receive, any other refused. Owner arms: 0x00 CheckSig by the owner key; 0x01 a 32-byte key whose unkeyed BLAKE3 is the owner, then its signature (97 bytes exactly); 0x02 the same with a 33-byte ECDSA key (98 bytes); 0x03 the input named by a one-byte index spends the version-0 P2SH of the owner; 0x04 an input carrying the owner as its covenant id is present (empty witness); 0x05-0xff refused. Borrowed receive: scheme 0x00 refused; 0x01 an empty witness and a threshold read as the guard's first 8 bytes as a signed int, clamped to 0 when negative; 0x02 CheckSig by the guard key; 0x03 a 129-byte witness whose BLAKE3(next || one-time key) equals the guard, the key signing and next becoming the successor's guard (rules.hash_chain 'keyed' names this key-committing link of kccs #18; the hash itself is unkeyed BLAKE3); any other scheme refused; successor 0 keeps the owner, owner scheme, borrow scheme and class, carries the expected guard, grows by strictly more than the threshold and keeps at least the input's KAS. transfer_delegator (fd3ef14a): not the leader, at least two family inputs, no outputs of its own, the leader authenticated as this template, its own owner authorized as above without a path byte. Any other tag ends in OP_RETURN. Issuers: PublicMint.mint(recipient_state, gen__kcc20_prefix, gen__kcc20_suffix) issues 0 < amount <= min(mint_amount, remaining) under the minter's extension commitment with supported schemes, continues as itself with remaining reduced by the amount at the same KAS, and validates the recipient output as the KCC20 template from the passed halves (which must hash to the minter's kcc20 template field) around that field and the recipient state; TokenSeed.create does the same with an amount of exactly zero and continues unchanged; split, reclaim, reclaim_into and reclaim_delegator move or retire allowance and deposits without creating token cells, PublicMint.reclaim and both reclaim_delegator entries under the retiring owner's signature. Engine: crates/kascov-labkit/src/kcc20_reference.rs runs every rule above on the real Kaspa script engine with the covenant context (rusty-kaspa 98a4ccd); every program it runs is chain bytes, and every check was attributed by ablation: with that check alone replaced by OpNop, or for a redundant group the whole group ({278, 295, 1662}, {1619, 1858, 2674}, {1637, 2663}, {1626, 3820}), the shape it refuses passes. That covers all five owner schemes as leader and as delegate, all four borrow schemes including a two-step hash chain with real keys, every official KCC-20 vector case, one to three inputs and outputs, the KAS floor, every issuer entry and cross-actor mixing. The program refused, among others: an unknown tag, a third delegate, a fourth output, a family output the leader does not authorise, a declared state with no cell, a negative, unsupported-scheme or reclassed successor, an unconserved total in either direction, an invalid path byte, a foreign signature in every signed arm, a key that does not hash to a p2pkh owner, an authority input that is not the owner script or covenant, trailing witness bytes, a disabled or unassigned borrow, a threshold-equal increase, a chain link that does not match or the right link signed by another key, a borrowed successor that changes owner, scheme or guard or loses KAS, swapped or forged continuations, a fabricated leader posing as this template, a mint of zero or over the limit or the allowance, a create of one, a minter or seed continuation that keeps its allowance or moves its KAS, and an issuer reclaim at the wrong position or with a partner whose template is not the one the issuer's state names. Eight chain spends were re-run under their own signature scripts and committed budgets and accepted: testnet-10 f13f6ce0 (a borrowed leader and a p2sh delegator), 7fa12aa5 (mint), 05060a38 (create), be4aaaec (PublicMint.split), 61636e17 (reclaim_into), bb9c3ecf (TokenSeed.split), d1574a60 (TokenSeed.reclaim) and mainnet df027ac6 (a covenant-owned leader). kascov's check_family agreed with the engine on the 12 shapes tried whose verdict does not hang on a signature, and check_issue proved every chain mint and create the engine accepted. Not claimed: signature validity stays consensus's (kascov's reader does not re-run sighash on chain data; the signed entries ran on synthetic, really signed transactions only). How kascov reads tokens of this build: from the genesis group forward, as the app's README asks of its readers, and only through the programs this pin describes. A token whose genesis or issuance kascov cannot prove stays unvalidated, never verified. A genesis output no spend has revealed yet is proven only by a rebuild (genesis_rebuild): this build's reviewed TokenSeed with the owner key and class that the genesis transaction's own proven outputs carry and its two template fields set to this build and to the seed itself, or this build's KCC20 cell with an owner taken from a proven output of the genesis or from a covenant the genesis spent with this build's template halves in its arguments, and an amount among the numbers that covenant or the genesis's proven outputs carry; the output is proven only when exactly one such rebuild commits to it byte for byte. Any other never-spent genesis output (a PublicMint, whose allowance nothing in the genesis determines, say) stays dark until its first spend; an issue made through an issuer this pin does not describe (the b782466 rebuilds above, or another app's issuer such as argent build dc96afcd... on mainnet) is not read as an issue until that issuer is pinned; and a cell whose state kascov does not read proves nothing. kascov reads the canonical encodings KCC-1 asks of a spender, and a reveal in any other encoding is not read, so its token reads unvalidated, never invalid. A token of this build is shown as a KCC-20 token only once it is verified; until then kascov names the build as reviewed and says the token is not proven yet.
